1. (Currently amended) Apparatus for inspection, comprising: an imaging assembly, comprising a plurality of cameras, which are mounted in different, respective locations in the imaging assembly and are adjusted to capture respective images of a sample; a motion assembly, which is configured to move at least one of the imaging assembly and the sample so as to cause the imaging assembly to scan the sample with a scan accuracy that is limited by a predetermined position tolerance; and an image processor, which is coupled to receive and process the images captured by the cameras so as to locate a defect in the sample with a position accuracy that is at least finer than the position tolerance.

4. (Currently amended) The apparatus according to claim 3, wherein the images comprise pixels having a pitch, and wherein the image processor is configured to compute the respective relative offsets with a precision that is at least finer than the pitch, and to combine the images using the respective relative offsets to produce a combined image having a resolution finer than the pitch, while ensuring that the combined image maintains the integrity of visual data represented therein.

6. (Currently amended) The apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the image processor is configured to recover a virtual position clock responsively to a periodic pattern on the sample that appears in the respective images captured by at least one of the cameras and to relative movement between the sample and the imaging assembly that is applied by the motion assembly during scanning, and to use the virtual position clock in registering the respective images with one another while accounting for potential variations in relative positioning.

18. (Currently amended) The method according to claim 17, wherein the images comprise pixels having a pitch, and wherein computing the respective relative offsets comprises determining the respective relative offsets with a precision that is at least finer than the pitch, and wherein processing the images comprises effectively combining the images using the respective relative offsets to produce a combined image having a resolution finer than the pitch, enabling enhanced defect resolution.

20. (Currently amended) The method according to claim 15, wherein processing the images comprises recovering a virtual position clock responsively to a periodic pattern on the sample that appears in the respective images captured by at least one of the cameras and to relative movement between the sample and the imaging assembly while scanning the sample, using the virtual position clock in effectively registering the respective images with one another while addressing possible discrepancies in positional accuracy. 

23. (Currently amended) The method according to claim 15, wherein the plurality of the cameras comprises at least twenty cameras, wherein the selection of cameras is made such that their effective coverage ensures enhanced imaging capabilities and defect detection accuracy. 

26. (Currently amended) The method according to claim 15, wherein the sample is scanned by the imaging assembly in a scan direction, and wherein the method comprises repositioning at least one post-inspection camera in a direction transverse to the scan direction while the imaging assembly scans the sample so as to position the at least one post-inspection camera over an area of the defect located by the image processor, and capturing an image of the area of the defect using the at least one post-inspection camera, while maintaining the focus on the detected defect without disturbance to the sample. 

27. (Currently amended) The method according to claim 26, wherein capturing the image comprises computing an error signal that is indicative of a deviation of movement of the imaging assembly relative to an ideal motion model with the aim to improve imaging accuracy, and driving the at least one post-inspection camera to image the area of the defect responsively to the error signal, thereby ensuring precise alignment in image capture.
